description: The tree a host DRAWS, built from authored data alone (US-3 of `123-skill-trees-and-progression`). This is the artifact that says a skill panel is a VALUE core returns and not a callback core invokes: `docs/module-contract.md` §3 forbids a UI hook on the C ABI, so what four engines share is this view-model and what differs is how each of them paints it. Each case carries the whole input — every authored tree, every authored skill, the fully resolved SkillTuning, and one actor’s levels, bank, pools, taken nodes and the two answers only a KB can give. Nothing in the expected output is authored twice: a node’s row (`depth`, and the `rows` a host lays out from) is derived from the authored parent edges rather than from a `tier` field that can disagree with them, a `label` falls back to the node’s own id so a half-authored tree is still inspectable, and `edges` is the same authored structure read the other way. `refusal` is the one place all five rungs of SKILL_UNLOCK_REFUSALS can appear, because the view is handed the KB’s two answers rather than guessing them. Regenerate with `npm run skill-resolution-corpus`.

cases.name: a-brand-new-character-opens-the-panel
cases.note: Nothing learned, nothing banked, nothing funded. Every node is refused `points` except the one the world priced at nothing, which is available out of an empty pool — the panel’s hardest state, and the one a port that special-cases “no progress yet” never draws.

cases.name: a-tree-partway-up
cases.note: Two levels, a funded pool, the root taken. The row after it is open, the row after THAT is available and conditional, and `spent` reads back what the taken nodes cost — so a panel can show a pool without re-deriving it.

cases.name: the-KB’s-two-answers-reach-the-panel
cases.note: The view is the one place both rules-layer rungs appear, because the view is HANDED them: an unmet authored goal reads `requires` and a prohibited node reads `forbidden`, in the ladder’s own order. A pure resolution may pin neither.

cases.name: a-capped-skill-still-draws-its-tree
cases.note: At the cap the price is zeroed and `nextLevel` holds — a panel that printed the cost of a level nobody can take would be inventing a number. The nodes are unaffected: a capped skill is still spent from its pool.

cases.name: a-tree-under-a-world-that-tunes-everything
cases.note: The same authored trees under `STEEP`: a different default node cost, a different cap for the skill with none of its own, a different curve. Not one number of the panel is core’s.

cases.name: a-world-with-no-trees-at-all
cases.note: The empty case, which is the shape of every world that did not select this module: an empty panel rather than a crash, and nothing for a host to draw.
